role_summary: Hands-on, research-facing IC4 who turns frontier AI lab goals into frontier-quality datasets, RL environments, evaluation harnesses, and validation systems. Owns data and environment quality for one or more capability areas by translating ambiguous model-improvement goals into task specs, rubrics, validators, and measurable lift, while partnering closely with researchers, engineers, QAs, and data creators. This is not a pure research, annotation-ops, or app-layer GenAI role; the bar is builder-level depth in data quality, environment design, training-adjacent systems, or evaluation methodology.
instructions: Evaluate against the Colombia IC4 role defined in the generic Frontier Data Lead JD. The candidate does not need Bay Area-level managerial scope; the hard bar is hands-on builder depth plus research-facing data and evaluation judgment.

Strong candidates usually anchor in at least one of these lanes: RL or post-training systems, coding-agent or SWE evaluation, tool-use or browser-use or MCP environments, data-quality and validation systems, multimodal or STEM reasoning data, or embodied or simulation infrastructure.

Do not over-index on exact titles like Frontier Data Lead. Adjacent titles such as Research Engineer, ML Engineer, Applied Scientist, AI Engineer, Data Scientist, Staff Software Engineer, and Technical Lead can fit if the underlying work is training-adjacent, evaluation-heavy, or environment-building.

The deepest false-positive pool in Colombia is BPO and outsourcing annotation work. AI Trainer, RLHF Specialist, and Data Quality Analyst titles at Teleperformance, Concentrix, TTEC, TaskUs, Alorica, TELUS International, Outlier, or similar vendors should default to NO unless the profile clearly shows rubric design, validation tooling, or methodology ownership.

A second major noise pattern is generic GenAI application work: RAG chatbots, copilots, automation flows, or AI transformation consulting without model-improvement, environment, benchmark, verifier, or data-quality-system ownership.

Because Colombia is a smaller market, do not require frontier-lab pedigree. Colombian university labs, corporate R&D teams, and strong ML groups at companies like Rappi, Mercado Libre, Globant, Habi, Addi, Nubank, Truora, or Bancolombia can all produce fits if the actual work crosses below the application layer.

Academic and research profiles should be treated seriously when they show simulation, verifiable STEM reasoning, multimodal evaluation, RL environments, or real model-training or evaluation methodology. Purely theoretical or teaching-only profiles still need a systems or data bridge.

At facial stage, ambiguous ML titles in strong Colombia or LATAM tech companies should usually pass through for full evaluation. Use the full profile to separate applied business ML from post-training, eval, or data-quality engineering.

For GitHub, prioritize repos and files that show eval harnesses, validators, benchmarks, synthetic data or task generation, RL environments, repo sandboxes, simulation code, reward or verifier logic, or fine-tuning or training utilities. De-emphasize prompt packs, notebook-only demos, and thin wrappers over hosted APIs.
search_priorities: RL, post-training, verifier, and environment builders in Colombia or Colombia-based LATAM teams
Coding-agent, SWE-benchmark, repo-sandbox, and code-evaluation builders
Tool-use, browser-use, MCP, and workflow-environment builders with explicit evaluation or quality systems
Data-quality, validation, synthetic-data, and LLM-evaluation builders who improved model behavior through better data
Multimodal, STEM-reasoning, or embodied and simulation researchers and engineers with strong implementation depth
Colombian academic and corporate R&D profiles whose research translates into evaluation, simulation, model-training, or environment-design work
Strong ML engineers at Colombian or regional tech companies who moved below the application layer into fine-tuning, evaluation, or training-data systems
intake_notes: The Colombia role uses the shared Frontier Data Lead generic JD, which is an IC4 or early-IC5-shaped hands-on role rather than the Bay Area senior-builder brief. The existing Colombia v3 brief already captured the most important market-specific traps, especially BPO annotation noise and smaller-market academic concentration. This v4 refresh keeps those Colombia calibrations but imports sharper role translation from the Bay Area Code + RL brief and the generic JD: the true bar is not generic applied AI or title pedigree, but hands-on work designing or improving environments, data-quality systems, evaluation harnesses, validators, synthetic data pipelines, or model-training-adjacent workflows. Strong candidates may anchor in one lane rather than all of them, but they should read as credible builders below the application layer.

capability_areas.name: 1. RL Environments, Verifiers & Post-Training Data Systems
capability_areas.description: Designing or building RL and post-training systems that improve frontier models through environments, verifiers, reward logic, preference data, or realistic long-horizon workflows. This is the clearest direct-fit lane for the RL Gyms side of the role.
builder_signals: Built or contributed to RLHF, DPO, GRPO, PPO, or similar post-training pipelines
Designed reward models, preference-collection workflows, verifier logic, or trajectory scoring
Built RL or agent environments, simulators, task suites, or realistic workflow interfaces
Created seed data, schemas, APIs, or synthetic trajectories for post-training or environment realism
Can explain how environment, reward, or data design changed model behavior or benchmark outcomes
user_signals: Mentioned RL or RLHF only as a skill keyword, course topic, or marketing term with no project evidence
Used a pre-trained RLHF-tuned model via API without participating in reward, environment, or evaluation design
Managed preference annotation work without designing the methodology

Created repo-level evaluation harnesses, patch verification, unit-test generation, or code-task validators
Designed training-data or synthetic-task pipelines for code-generation or software-engineering models
Built coding agents that operate on real repositories or long-horizon development tasks
Analyzed failure modes on software-engineering tasks and used that analysis to improve the benchmark, data, or model
user_signals: Used Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT, or Claude Code for development without building benchmarks, evals, or improvement loops around them
Built standard CI, devtools, or backend infrastructure with no model-evaluation or code-generation component
Created codegen demos or wrappers without task realism, verification, or dataset methodology

capability_areas.description: Building simulation environments, synthetic data, or physically grounded interaction systems for embodied or VLA-style agents. Lower-volume than the other lanes in Colombia, but still directly relevant when the work shows environment realism and measurable evaluation depth.
builder_signals: Built simulation environments for robot or embodied-agent training

Created sim-to-real transfer frameworks, evaluation suites, or long-horizon task environments

Worked on perception-only subsystems with no evidence of interaction, task design, or environment quality work

depth_distinction.builder_definition: A builder for this role personally defines the data or environment that changes model behavior: task suites, rubrics, validators, reward or verifier logic, synthetic generators, evaluation harnesses, or fine-tuning loops. They can explain how better data, better realism, better validation, or better task design turned into measurable lift, fewer failure modes, or stronger coverage. Hands-on means they authored or directly shaped code, methodology, and quality criteria themselves.
depth_distinction.user_definition: A user or adjacent profile builds on top of models or around the serving layer without shaping the data, evaluation, or improvement loop. This includes generic RAG and chatbot builders, model-serving or MLOps teams with no training or evaluation ownership, annotation operators following existing rubrics, and managers who coordinate the work but do not design the technical quality system.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: CODING-AGENT SPECIALISTS: Strong fit even without explicit RL titles if they built real SWE benchmarks, repo sandboxes, patch verification, unit-test generation, or code-task post-training loops. RL OR SIMULATION SPECIALISTS: Strong fit even without coding-agent titles if they designed environments, verifiers, tasks, or proof-of-value loops that improved model behavior. ACADEMICS: Research profiles can fit when the work is implementable and systems-facing, not purely theoretical. BPO OR OPS PROFILES: Only save when the person clearly designed rubrics, validators, quality metrics, or evaluation pipelines rather than merely following them. CAREER TRANSITIONERS: Evaluate on current hands-on model-improvement work, not on whether the entire career has carried the same title.

inferential_save_rules.description: For profiles where evidence is sparse but priors are strong, SAVE with a flag rather than reject on insufficient evidence. These candidates should be reviewed by the recruiter instead of being silently lost.
conditions: PhD in ML, AI, CS, EE, physics, mathematics, statistics, robotics, or another quantitative field plus a current technical ML, AI, research-engineering, or simulation-heavy role even if bullets are sparse
Current technical role at a frontier lab, strong AI company, or serious Colombian research lab with title or team context suggesting training, evaluation, agents, benchmarks, or simulation work
Visible progression from SWE, data, robotics, or research roles into a current ML or AI role with direct model-improvement signals even if profile detail is thin
Sparse profile but clear open-source, publication, or headline evidence of RL environments, evaluation systems, coding-agent work, or fine-tuning
inferential_save_rules.note: These are not confident saves. They are too strong to reject on missing detail and should be prioritized for human review.

strong_saves.name: RL environment researcher or builder
strong_saves.why: Direct environment-design and RL signal maps cleanly to the highest-priority capability lane.

strong_saves.name: Regional platform ML engineer with fine-tuning or eval depth
strong_saves.why: Large-scale production ML plus clear evidence below the application layer.

incorrect_saves.name: BPO AI trainer or RLHF annotation operator

incorrect_saves.name: RPA or automation consultant with AI marketing language

incorrect_saves.name: AI transformation consultant or cloud architect without builder evidence

borderline_verify.name: Bank or marketplace data scientist with explicit fine-tuning or eval signals

borderline_verify.name: Academic RL or simulation profile with sparse implementation detail

borderline_verify.name: Applied CV or speech engineer with real training and evaluation depth
borderline_verify.why: Do not reject purely because the domain is not LLM-native when the builder-level data, benchmark, or simulation depth is real.

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure data analytics or BI
non_fit_patterns.description: Data analysts and BI professionals building dashboards, reports, ad hoc SQL, and business reporting for human stakeholders.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Their data work is reporting and visualization, not training data, evaluation design, or model-quality improvement.
examples: BI analyst building Tableau or Power BI dashboards
Analytics engineer building dbt models for finance reporting
Data analyst writing SQL for marketing or growth teams

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure software engineering with no ML component
non_fit_patterns.description: Backend, frontend, mobile, or full-stack engineers building applications or infrastructure with zero visible ML, evaluation, or research layer across their career.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Software engineering is helpful, but without evidence of ML work, training data, evaluation methodology, or model-improvement systems, the role's core competency is missing.
examples: Full-stack engineer building React and Node applications
Backend engineer building REST APIs and microservices
Mobile engineer building iOS or Android apps

non_fit_patterns.label: MLOps or model serving without training or evaluation ownership
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers who deploy, monitor, and scale models in production but do not design training data, fine-tuning, environments, or evaluation systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: They operate around the model rather than shaping the post-training, data-quality, or quality-loop work this role owns.
examples: MLOps engineer managing SageMaker or Kubeflow
ML platform engineer building feature stores or serving infrastructure
DevOps engineer who happens to deploy ML workloads

non_fit_patterns.label: Data engineering or ETL without ML awareness
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers building data pipelines, warehouses, and transformations for analytics or business operations rather than model training or evaluation.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: They move data but do not design it for model behavior, training quality, or evaluation rigor.
examples: Data engineer building Spark pipelines for a warehouse
ETL developer building Airflow DAGs for reporting
Warehouse engineer optimizing analytics tables

non_fit_patterns.label: Generic GenAI or RAG application builders
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers or consultants who shipped copilots, chat workflows, AI assistants, or automation tools for end users without owning post-training, benchmark design, verifier logic, or data-quality systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: They are building on top of models rather than improving models through data, environments, or evaluation methodology. The role sits below the application layer.
examples: Enterprise copilot builder using APIs and RAG only
Consultant shipping AI automation workflows with no eval or data-system ownership
Prompt-engineering product builder with no training or benchmark work

non_fit_patterns.label: Annotation or data-ops execution only
non_fit_patterns.description: People who label data, review outputs, or manage annotation operations without creating the rubric, validation tooling, or quality system.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: This role designs the process and technical quality bar; it is not an annotation-operations role.
examples: AI trainer following existing RLHF rubrics
Annotation QA specialist checking labels for throughput
Data-ops lead focused on staffing and queue management

non_fit_patterns.label: BPO or outsourcing annotation work
non_fit_patterns.description: High-volume Colombia market pattern where AI, data-quality, or RLHF titles appear at outsourcing vendors whose actual work is operational annotation, moderation, or review.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The title contains ML vocabulary, but the work is following rubrics at scale rather than designing training pipelines, reward systems, validation tooling, or evaluation infrastructure.
examples: AI Trainer at Teleperformance doing RLHF annotation
RLHF Specialist at Concentrix rating model outputs
Data Quality Analyst at TELUS International following labeling rubrics

non_fit_patterns.label: Project, program, or people management without technical IC work
non_fit_patterns.description: Managers, PMs, and coordinators who organize ML or data teams but do not personally write code, shape quality systems, or design technical methodology.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role requires hands-on technical leadership, not managerial oversight alone.
examples: Technical program manager for an ML team
Product manager for an AI product
Engineering manager with no recent technical authorship

non_fit_override_rule: A non-fit pattern is overridden when the profile shows concrete builder-level evidence in a capability area. Someone at a BPO who designed rubrics, validators, or evaluation pipelines is not annotation noise. Someone at a bank or marketplace who fine-tuned models, built evals, or designed training-data systems is not generic applied ML. Actual evidence in the work history always beats the default expectation from the company or title.

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: Any technical role touching training, agents, evaluation, data, research engineering, or model-improvement systems is a strong signal. Pure manager-only profiles still need adjacency evidence, but employer signal is very strong.

Need at least one visible sign of training, evaluation, agents, data quality, simulation, or post-training depth. Company signal helps, but these employers also contain adjacent product and platform roles.

Need publications, open-source work, research detail, or hands-on model or simulation work showing evaluation, training, benchmark, or environment-building depth. Title alone at a university is not sufficient because teaching-only and administrative roles exist.

ML roles at these companies range from pure applied business ML to genuinely training-adjacent work. Do not reject on company alone. At facial stage, ML titles here are usually ambiguous YES; at full stage, the decision must be based on the actual work in the bullets.
Same standard as any candidate: capability-area mapping plus builder-vs-user depth based on real profile evidence.

minimum_bar_description: 4+ years of total ML-adjacent experience, which can include software engineering roles with real ML components, ML research, data science with model building, simulation-heavy robotics work, or ML engineering. This does not require 4 years specifically in post-training, RLHF, or evaluation. A software engineer with 6 years total and 1.5 years of direct fine-tuning or benchmark work meets the bar. A career transitioner with 3 years of infrastructure work and 1 year of hands-on RLHF, evaluation, or simulation-environment work can also meet it if the current role is directly relevant. The floor exists to filter out junior career starters, not to penalize non-linear trajectories into model-improvement work.

domain_depth_objects: task suites with measurable model lift
reward or verifier logic for long-horizon agent behavior
benchmark or evaluation harnesses for code, tool-use, or multimodal tasks

transferability_examples.source_context: Applied CV or speech ML engineer with large-scale training, data curation, and evaluation ownership
transferability_examples.target_context: Frontier data quality, multimodal, or STEM reasoning lane
transferability_examples.rationale: The core transferable skill is builder-level authorship of training data, evaluation, and model-improvement methodology, not whether the model family is already LLM-native.

transferability_examples.source_context: Robotics or simulation engineer who built RL environments, validators, or long-horizon tasks
transferability_examples.target_context: RL gyms, embodied, or tool-use environment work
transferability_examples.rationale: Environment realism, verifier logic, and trajectory design transfer directly when the work already shaped agent behavior rather than merely consuming a simulator.

transferability_examples.source_context: RAG or copilot application engineer using hosted APIs with no benchmark, fine-tuning, or quality-system ownership
transferability_examples.rationale: Application-layer AI delivery does not demonstrate the below-the-application-layer data, environment, or evaluation depth this role requires.

worked_examples.profile: ML Engineer & AI Researcher, Universidad de los Andes (MSc Biomedical Eng), Bogota. AI Research Engineer @ UniAndes: created a segmentation benchmark dataset from 6 years of satellite imagery and validated SOTA models to establish performance baselines; re-benchmarked with VLMs for open-ended regional recognition. Graduate Research Assistant: built a benchmark + multitask model for robotic-surgery scene understanding (instance/semantic segmentation, action recognition, phase recognition), beating SOTA; multimodal fetal-echocardiography model surpassing image-only by 14%. Domain is medical / remote-sensing CV, not LLM. Google DeepMind Scholar. [Santiago R., conf 0.62]
worked_examples.reasoning: Step 1 (capability map): benchmark design + multimodal model training + VLM evaluation maps to capability area 4 (Data Quality, Validation & Synthetic Data) and area 5 (Multimodal & STEM Reasoning Data). Step 2 (depth test): builder, not user — he authored the benchmark dataset, designed the multitask model, and can tie design choices to measurable lift (14%, >5% over SOTA). That is the builder_definition: personally defines the data/eval that changes model behavior. Step 3 (transferability): the domain is adjacent (medical/remote-sensing CV, not LLM post-training), but benchmark-design and VLM-evaluation methodology transfer directly to multimodal and evaluation work. Weigh: real below-the-application-layer methodology depth clears the bar; the adjacency is a recruiter-deep-dive question on LLM-native adaptability, not a reason to reject. Decision: SAVE (0.62) — solid, with a deep-dive flag, not a hedge.

worked_examples.profile: Deputy Director of Data Mining @ Quantil; Senior Fellow Responsible AI @ BID Lab; Adjunct Professor (Design & Analysis of Algorithms) @ UniAndes. MSc Systems Eng + BSc Mathematics (UniAndes). DeepMind-CINFONIA scholarship. Work: NLP model development and fairness/responsible-AI evaluation methodology; leads applied DS/AI projects for clients. No direct post-training, RL-environment, coding-agent, or LLM fine-tuning evidence. [Melissa Robles, conf 0.52]
worked_examples.reasoning: Step 1 (capability map): NLP model development + fairness evaluation methodology gestures at area 4 (Data Quality, Validation) and the evaluation side of the role. Step 2 (depth test): genuinely research-facing and builder-leaning — she develops models and designs evaluation methodology, above the pure-application line. But the evidence is about responsible-AI / fairness evaluation, not the post-training / environment / benchmark systems the role centers on. Step 3 (transferability): fairness-eval and NLP model work could transfer to data-quality and evaluation work, but the bridge is unproven on the profile. Weigh: stronger than a reject (real methodology depth) but the core-lane evidence is indirect — so SAVE-with-a-transfer-flag rather than a clean SAVE. Decision: TRANSFERABLE_SAVE (0.52) — flag for recruiter to probe the depth of the NLP / model-training work before committing.

worked_examples.profile: AI Software Engineer @ Bancolombia (progression: AI Jr -> Senior -> Specialist Architect -> SW Engineer, 2023-present). MSc Computer Engineering + BSc Biomedical Eng (UniAndes). Skills: Python, TensorFlow, AWS, ML, anomaly detection, big data. Profile is SPARSE — titles and a clear AI role progression, but almost no bullet detail on what the work actually was. [Nicolas Laverde, conf 0.42]
worked_examples.reasoning: Step 1 (capability map): can't map cleanly — the profile names AI roles at a bank but gives no project detail, so no capability area is evidenced directly. Step 2 (depth test): indeterminate; no discriminating practitioner signals either way (could be real model work, could be applied business ML on top of vendors). Step 3 (transferability): n/a without evidence. Weigh: this is exactly the inferential_save_rules case — sparse profile but strong priors (UniAndes MSc, a multi-year AI role progression at a serious employer). Rejecting on thin evidence would silently lose a possibly-real builder; the rule says SAVE-with-a-flag and route to recruiter. Decision: INFERENTIAL_SAVE (0.42) — recruiter to verify whether the Bancolombia work involves any model-training, evaluation, or data-quality-system depth vs. applied business ML.

worked_examples.profile: GCP | Data Science | AI/ML Engineer | Python | ML | GenerativeAI, UniAndes. Engineering Lead: built a stateful autonomous conversational AI agent on Dialogflow CX for customer diagnostics/booking. Senior LLM Developer (consultant) @ Walmart: AI-driven financial automation. GenAI Professor @ Simplilearn (taught GANs, VAEs, Transformers). Startup founder. Plus BPO-adjacent Scale AI annotation work. Skills: MLOps, Google Gemini, Generative AI Tools, Transformers, Vertex, Contact Center / CCaaS. [Jaime Saldarriaga, conf 0.92]
worked_examples.reasoning: Step 1 (capability map): on keywords this looks like the strongest profile in the set — LLM developer, Transformers, GenAI, annotation, Scale AI all surface-match multiple capability areas. Step 2 (depth test): apply the builder-vs-user line and it collapses. Every concrete bullet is integration and application — a Dialogflow CX conversational agent, LLM-API automation, RAG/chatbot delivery, teaching GenAI, contact-center architecture. The Scale AI work is annotation, not annotation-methodology design. This is two non_fit_patterns at once: Generic GenAI or RAG application builders and BPO or outsourcing annotation work. Step 3 (transferability): nothing to port — there is no evaluation system, RL environment, fine-tuning pipeline, benchmark, or data-quality infrastructure he authored. Weigh: the case-for is pure keyword surface; the case-against is the total absence of below-the-application-layer methodology. Decision: REJECT at high confidence (0.92). This is the floor — more AI vocabulary than any of the three saves, and the lowest actual fit, because the role sits below the application layer and none of this work does.
